full_judgment:
2. The respondent No.9 and the petitioner filed the suit for declaration that the ex parte decree passed on 13-7-1982 in Other Class Suit No.1379 of 1980 in favour of the respondent Nos. 1-8 is void, fraudulent and not 'binding upon the plaintiff and described the suit land in schedule 'Kha' to the plaintiffs suit as a tank consisting of .65 decimals appertaining to 65 Khatian No.1114, plot No.2808 . within Mouza Sherpur, District Jamalpur. That it is stated that the suit land described in the respondents suit being No.1379 of 180 is 65 decimals CS Khatian No.1114, plot No.2808 within Mouza Sherpur, District Jamalpur; that in the valuation statement the land has been described as paddy producing land and it has not been described as a tank. That the case of the petitioner as the plaintiff, in short, is that in Other Suit No.1379 of 1980 the Government was not made party and only the Sub- Divisional Officer was made party and in that suit there was a false claim that the schedule property belonged to Tazammel Huq Chowdhury who has got settlement from the Sudangshu Kanta Acharjee. No summon was served upon the Government and the Government was not aware of the decree passed in that suit and the same is liable to be declared illegal and void. The suit land is a pond not under the control and management of Sherpur Pourshava, when the defendant filed application for mutation on 25-9-1985 and later on the plaintiff could know about the earlier decree only on 19-1-1987. 

 3. The respondent Nos.1-8 contested the suit filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the original owner Sudhanshu Kumar Acherjee being owner and in khas possession of the pond ultimately settled to Tazammel Huq Chowdhury on 12 Chaitra 1351 BS and he being in possession the record was wrongly done in favour of the Government for which Other Suit No.1379 of 1980 was filed and the notice of the suit was regularly served upon the Government and the suit was decreed and, as such, the plaintiff's objection to the said suit is not tenable. 

 6. The suit land is being admittedly a tank and, as such, non-retainable land of the Zamindars the plaintiff of Other Class Suit No.1379 of 1980 could not claim the land on the basis of alleged settlement from the ex-landlord under the provision of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 8. No issue was suggested or framed and no pleading or evidence was advanced on behalf of the defendant that the suit land being a tank is not retainable and, as such, could not be the subject-matter of settlement by the original landlord.
